source.title: Early-stopped neural networks are consistent
source.authors: Zi-Wei Ji; Justin D. Li; Matus Telgarsky

record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical generalization guarantees for early-stopped shallow ReLU networks and a theoretical counterexample for local interpolation; it does not test the listed claim versions' interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test fitting random labels, width sweeps, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Its MNIST results concern frozen random-feature predictors, not the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study proves consistency with early stopping and inconsistency of certain univariate interpolants, but tests none of V1–V8. Increasing width together with sample size and training time does not test V2's width effect beyond zero training error; the authors explicitly leave their result's application to interpolating neural networks open.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors prove arbitrarily small excess population logistic risk, classification risk, and calibration error for early-stopped shallow ReLU gradient descent, and almost-sure consistency under specified schedules. Their interpolation lower bound requires particular noisy univariate distributional assumptions and does not establish that early stopping is necessary for trained neural networks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes early stopping and consistency theoretically, rather than testing the listed studies' methods or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Theoretical bounds depend on width, sample size, temperature, optimization accuracy, stopping radius, and the complexity of the reference model; the illustrative MNIST tasks have different reported test errors.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1.1 bounds excess population logistic risk; Corollary 2.3 proves almost-sure consistency in logistic risk, classification risk, and conditional probability estimation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early-stopped shallow ReLU networks trained by gradient descent are statistically consistent under the specified schedules and bounded-input assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Frozen random-feature predictors attain approximately 0.01 test error on MNIST 1 versus 5 and 0.08 on MNIST 3 versus 5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frozen random-feature predictors can achieve low test error on these binary MNIST tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Local interpolation rules have classification risk bounded a positive constant above Bayes risk under the noisy univariate distributional assumptions in Lemma B.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local interpolation can prevent statistical consistency on certain noisy univariate classification distributions.

record.problems: The central results are theoretical. The empirical illustration reports only two MNIST task errors, with no stated uncertainty or exact width; it does not evaluate the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architectures and recipes; chance performance on held-out random labels.
Test-error changes from widening networks beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and its dependence on tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes, dropout strengths, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not judgments against the validity of the paper's separate theoretical results. The cited original studies motivate concern about generalization bounds; their findings are not independently tested here.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under the same recipes on natural labels.
Width beyond interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with training set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.operation_detail: Theorem 1.1 bounds population logistic excess risk for an iterate selected with small empirical risk and norm, under stated parameter and sampling conditions.

conditions.value: arbitrary binary classification distribution with bounded inputs; Bayes risk need not be zero
vanilla gradient descent on inner weights with constant step size η=4/ρ²
early-stopped iterate; theorem also allows Rgd=∞

rows.measure: Population logistic excess risk R(W≤t)−R, bounded by the theorem's reference-model, optimization, and generalization terms.
rows.value: Theorem 1.1 bound; no single numeric value stated.
rows.note: A theoretical guarantee, not an empirical estimate of a train-test gap.
rows.check: A valid theoretical result, but its population-risk bound measures none of the listed versions. The recorded observed state cannot describe an effect on those versions.

rows.subject: early-stopped shallow ReLU networks
rows.operation_detail: Corollary 2.3 specifies gradient descent schedules and proves almost-sure convergence of population risk, classification risk, and conditional predictions.
rows.measure: Population logistic risk, classification risk, and L²(µx) conditional-model error.
rows.baseline: Bayes logistic risk R and Bayes classification risk Rz
rows.value: R(Ŵn)→R, Rz(Ŵn)→Rz, and φ̂n→py almost surely.
rows.note: The result concerns consistency as sample size grows, not a measured train-test gap.
rows.check: No listed version is measured. Correct the width schedule to m(n)=n^((40/3)(1−ξ)), rather than n^(40/(3(1−ξ))). Consistency jointly changes sample size, width, temperature, and training time.

rows.subject: univariate local interpolation rules Fn
rows.operation_detail: Proposition 1.3 lower-bounds population classification risk for rules that interpolate the sample and satisfy the stated local condition.

conditions.value: univariate noisy distribution; assumptions in Proposition 1.3

rows.measure: Population classification risk relative to Bayes classification risk
rows.uncertainty: Probability guarantee stated as at least 1−δ
rows.note: The proposition concerns local interpolation rules generally; it does not establish that the paper's trained networks satisfy that property.
rows.check: The lower bound does not measure a listed version or establish failure of trained neural networks. State the distributional assumptions supplied in Lemma B.1: continuous compactly supported marginal, continuous conditional label probability, and positive mass where that probability lies outside {0,1/2,1}. Noisy data alone is insufficient.
